value.title: ARM welcomes judgment on Pula Group litigation

value.title: Creecy says rail reforms on track as South Africa targets freight recovery
value.snippet: Transport Minister Barbara Creecy has expressed confidence in South Africa’s rail reform programme, highlighting that the government is committed to restoring the country’s rail network, attracting private investment and embedding reforms in law to ensure their continuity beyond the current administration. Creecy provided these insights during a Creamer Media transport webinar titled ‘Reform and Recovery: Are South Africa’s rail reforms taking shape and what’s next?’, held on October 14.

value.title: Deaths prompt South African miners' safety review, Minerals Council CEO says
value.snippet: South African miners are reviewing safety protocols as the number of fatalities this year is already above the last two, Minerals Council South Africa CEO Mzila Mthenjane told Reuters. Fifty-three deaths were recorded as of October 12, Mthenjane said, compared with historic lows of 41 in 2025 and 42 in 2024.

value.title: UK-based EnergyPathways works to commercialise hydrogen, graphite project early
value.snippet: Aim-listed UK energy transition company EnergyPathways is fast-tracking development of its low-carbon hydrogen and graphite production facility at Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria, with the aim of becoming revenue-generative by 2029. The project may potentially start up earlier, subject to further design optimisation and supply chain management.

value.title: Diatreme confirms world-class project potential at Northern Silica
value.snippet: ASX-listed Diatreme Resources' prefeasibility study (PFS) on the Northern Silica project in northern Queensland has confirmed its potential as a profitable, long-life and high-purity silica sand mine. The PFS outlines a Phase 1 startup of operations comprising three-million tonnes of capacity for a capital cost of $443-million, which estimates a before-tax net present value (NPV) of $1.29-billion, an internal rate of return (IRR) of 36%, a payback period of four years and life-of-mine (LoM) gross revenue of $8.1-billion.

value.title: Greenland-focused miners welcome Trump's plans for major mineral exploration
value.snippet: ASX-listed AuKing Mining and Nasdaq-listed Greenland Mines have both welcomed the strong commitment shown by the US government to advance critical mineral projects in Greenland. AuKing explains Greenland’s critical minerals sector is attracting increased strategic interest from the US, highlighted by President Donald Trump’s announcement on October 14 regarding plans for major mineral exploration activities in Greenland.

value.title: Aluminium heads for surplus in 2027 as supply shock fades
value.snippet: Aluminium is expected to swing into a surplus in 2027, potentially of more than one-million metric tons, as analysts eye a wave of new supply from Indonesia and a recovery in flows from Gulf smelters. Expectations for a supply bump have already helped push prices of the metal used in transport and packaging below $3 000 a ton this week to their lowest since December, after they hit four-year highs in June on trade disruptions from the Iran war and dwindling inventories.

value.title: Austrian investor rushes to boost copper production at old Chile mine

A review of documents from US-registered Global Critical Resources (GCR) showed the company is banking on a hybrid approach of boosting its own mine's production while continuing to supplement its supplies with ore mined by dozens of independent miners.

value.title: Australia's New Hope to fold Malabar Resources into $4.39bn coal group in all-scrip deal
value.snippet: Australian coal miner New Hope said on Monday it would acquire unlisted peer Malabar Resources in a deal valued at about A$2.4-billion ($1.67-billion), giving it full ownership of the Maxwell coal mine in New South Wales. Under the scheme of arrangement, Malabar shareholders will receive 0.5 New Hope shares for each Malabar share held, implying a value of A$2.92 per Malabar share based on New Hope's closing price on October 16.

value.title: Freeport bets on chemical solution to reach copper leaching target
value.snippet: Freeport-McMoRan is betting a new chemical compound can help it reach an ambitious target of extracting 800-million pounds of copper from waste rock each year and expand production beyond traditional mines to meet surging global demand. Working with a fleet of chemists, the world's largest publicly traded copper producer has spent the past three years testing dozens of chemical cocktails in the hopes of boosting the amount of copper it extracts, or leaches, from mine waste tailings piles that contain more than 40-billion pounds of copper.

value.title: Shenghe Resources says to sell majority stakes in some businesses

value.title: Africa's minerals value-add drive interests investors but faces energy hurdle

value.title: Startups are extracting more copper using microbes

value.title: Fortescue demonstrates effectiveness of world's first arsenic removal tech for copper

The patented Toowong Process uses a low-temperature, low-pressure hydrometallurgical method to separate arsenic from copper concentrate.

value.title: China aluminium output hits record quarterly high despite capacity cap
